findings.body:
The change removed the `if samples.is_empty() { return 0; }` guard. For an empty slice, `samples.iter().sum()` is 0 and `samples.len() as u32` is 0, so the new `total / samples.len() as u32` performs an integer division by zero. Rust panics on integer division by zero in all build modes, whereas the old code returned 0 before reaching the division.

Trigger: Calling average(&[]) or report(&[]), for example with a sample set that has no readings yet.

Impact: Any caller that passes an empty slice to `average` (directly or via `report`, which formats `average(samples)`) now panics instead of getting a mean of 0. This is a regression introduced by this change.
findings.suggestion: Restore the empty check: `if samples.is_empty() { return 0; }` before the division.
findings.title: Empty slice now panics with division by zero in average

risk_level.reason: The empty-slice guard was removed, so average now divides by zero and panics on empty input, and the public function has at least one caller elsewhere.
